def-ip-tv-functional-on-l2-distributiona:
## Definition

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be open and let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Every $u\in X$ is integrable on compact subsets by Cauchy–Schwarz. Define its extended distributional total variation by
$$TV_2(u;\Omega):=\sup\left\{\int_\Omega u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi\,dx:\ \varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^2),\ \sup_{x\in\Omega}|\varphi(x)|\le1\right\}\in[0,+\infty],$$
where $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^2)$ denotes smooth compactly supported vector fields, $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm, and $\operatorname{div}\varphi=\partial_1\varphi_1+\partial_2\varphi_2$. This definition treats $L^2$ functions as almost-everywhere classes and does not require $u\in L^1(\Omega)$.
def-ip-tv-level-set-representatives-and-:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Let $u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^2)$, with functions identified when they agree almost everywhere. For full-space TV, use $u$ itself. For a bounded-domain Dirichlet or Neumann problem, use the zero extension $\widetilde u$ only to define the geometric level sets; this does not change the selected regularizer, and for each nonzero level the resulting set lies inside $\Omega$. For $t>0$, the positive $t$-level class is the measurable-set class of $E_t^+(u):=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:u(x)>t\}$; for $t<0$, the negative $t$-level class is the class of $E_t^-(u):=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:u(x)<t\}$. These classes do not depend on the representative of $u$. For any measurable set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, its density-one representative is

$$E^{(1)}:=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{|E\cap B(x,r)|}{|B(x,r)|}=1\right\}.$$

This representative depends only on the almost-everywhere class of $E$. The canonical level set $U_u^{(t)}$ is $(E_t^+(u))^{(1)}$ when $t>0$ and $(E_t^-(u))^{(1)}$ when $t<0$. Its canonical boundary is the ordinary topological boundary $\partial U_u^{(t)}$ in $\mathbb R^2$. For two nonempty boundary sets, use the usual extended Hausdorff distance induced by Euclidean distance; set $d_H(\varnothing,\varnothing)=0$ and $d_H(E,F)=+\infty$ if exactly one set is empty. Hausdorff convergence uses this convention and is invariant under changes to a function on a null set.
def-ip-tv-variational-curvature:
## Definition

Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$ or let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Choose one of three perimeter functionals for measurable $E\subseteq\Omega$: full-space perimeter $P_R(E)=P(E;\mathbb R^2)$ when $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$; Neumann relative perimeter $P_N(E)=P(E;\Omega)$ on a bounded domain; or Dirichlet perimeter $P_D(E)=P(\widetilde E;\mathbb R^2)$, where $\widetilde E$ is $E$ extended by the empty set outside $\Omega$. Require finite measure and finite selected perimeter, and let $\kappa$ be measurable with $\int_F|\kappa|<\infty$ for every set considered. The set $E$ has **variational curvature** $\kappa$ for the selected model if its selected perimeter minus $\int_E\kappa\,dx$ is no greater than the same quantity for every finite-measure finite-selected-perimeter competitor $F\subseteq\Omega$ whose symmetric difference $F\mathbin\triangle E$ has compact closure in $\Omega$. In the full-space model, this means compact closure in $\mathbb R^2$.

For bounded Dirichlet TV, a separate **obstacle curvature** condition on $\Omega$ means that $\Omega$, viewed as a finite-perimeter set in $\mathbb R^2$, minimizes $F\mapsto P(F;\mathbb R^2)-\int_F\kappa_\Omega\,dx$ over all finite-measure finite-perimeter $F\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ whose symmetric difference with $\Omega$ has compact closure in $\mathbb R^2$.
lem-ip-tv-l2-finite-variation-has-radon-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. If $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is open, $u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, and $TV_2(u;\Omega)<\infty$, then each distributional derivative of $u$ is represented by a finite signed Radon measure. Their vector measure $Du$ has finite Radon variation and $|Du|(\Omega)=TV_2(u;\Omega)$.
lem-ip-tv-l2-functional-properties:
## Statement

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be open and let $TV_2(\cdot;\Omega)$ be the extended distributional total variation on $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. It is proper, convex, lower semicontinuous in the $L^2$ norm, and positively one-homogeneous for nonnegative scalars. For every $u\in BV(\Omega)\cap L^2(\Omega)$, it agrees with spatial TV: $TV_2(u;\Omega)=TV(u;\Omega)$.
def-ip-tv-dual-source-certificate:
## Definition

Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$, or let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Set $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ for a measure space $(\Sigma,\mu)$, using the real integral inner products. Let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, and let $A^*:Y\to X$ be its Hilbert adjoint, characterized by $\langle Au,p\rangle_Y=\langle u,A^*p\rangle_X$. Define $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ as follows. If $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$, take $R(u)=TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)$, the supremum of $\int u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi$ over smooth compactly supported vector fields of Euclidean norm at most one. For bounded $\Omega$, either take Neumann TV, $R(u)=TV(u;\Omega)$ when $u\in BV(\Omega)$ and $+\infty$ otherwise, or Dirichlet TV, $R(u)=TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^2)$ when the zero extension $\widetilde u$ belongs to $BV(\mathbb R^2)$ and $+\infty$ otherwise. Thus the bounded-domain choices count, respectively, only the interior derivative or also the jump of the zero extension across the boundary. In the full-space case finite $R$ does not require global $L^1$ integrability.

Identify each $q\in X$ with the continuous linear functional $h\mapsto\langle q,h\rangle_X$ by the real Hilbert-space Riesz representation. For exact data $f=Au^\dagger$, a **minimum-TV exact solution** is a point $u^\dagger\in X$ satisfying $Au^\dagger=f$ and $R(u^\dagger)\le R(u)$ for every $u\in X$ with $Au=f$. A vector $p^\dagger\in Y$ is a **dual source certificate** for $u^\dagger$ if $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$, where $\partial R$ is the convex subdifferential on the real Banach space $X$. The **TV source condition** at $u^\dagger$ is that such a certificate exists; it does not assert uniqueness of the truth or of the certificate. For a chosen certificate, the associated Bregman distance is

$$D_R^{A^*p^\dagger}(u,u^\dagger):=R(u)-R(u^\dagger)-\langle A^*p^\dagger,u-u^\dagger\rangle_X,$$

for $u\in\operatorname{dom}R$.
lem-ip-planar-isoperimetric-inequality-f:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Every Lebesgue-measurable set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ with finite area and finite perimeter satisfies
$$4\pi |E|\le P(E;\mathbb R^2)^2.$$
lem-ip-tv-l2-cutoff-approximation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. If $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ and $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)<\infty$, there exist smooth cutoffs $\chi_k$ with $0\le\chi_k\le1$, $\chi_k=1$ on $B(0,k)$, support in $B(0,2k)$, and $\sup_{k\ge1}k\|\nabla\chi_k\|_\infty<\infty$. For every family satisfying these four conditions, $v_k:=\chi_ku$ belongs to $BV(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^1(\mathbb R^2)$, has support in $B(0,2k)$, converges to $u$ in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$, and
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty}TV(v_k;\mathbb R^2)\le TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2).$$
lem-ip-tv-dual-attainment-and-certificat:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, and let $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be one of the full-space, Dirichlet, or Neumann TV functionals. Assume that $R$ is proper, convex, lower semicontinuous, and positively one-homogeneous, and that $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-$R$ exact solution of $Au=f$ with a dual source certificate $p^\dagger\in Y$, so $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Define $K:=\{p\in Y:A^*p\in\partial R(0)\}$ and $D_{\alpha,w}(p):=\langle f+w,p\rangle_Y-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|p\|_Y^2$ for $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$.

For each $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$, $D_{\alpha,w}$ has a unique maximizer $p_{\alpha,w}=\operatorname{Proj}_K((f+w)/\alpha)$. If $u_{\alpha,w}$ is any supplied global minimizer of $u\mapsto\frac12\|Au-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u)$, then $p_{\alpha,w}=(f+w-Au_{\alpha,w})/\alpha$, $A^*p_{\alpha,w}\in\partial R(u_{\alpha,w})$, and $A^*p_{\alpha,w}\in\partial R(0)$. For every such supplied minimizer, the correctly normalized primal-dual value identity is

$$\min_u\{\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w)\|_Y^2+\alpha R(u)\}=\alpha D_{\alpha,w}(p_{\alpha,w}).$$

Let $P_0:=\{p\in K:\langle f,p\rangle_Y=R(u^\dagger)\}$ and let $p_0$ be its unique minimum-norm element. For every sequence $\alpha_n>0$ with $\alpha_n\to0$, $p_{\alpha_n,0}\to p_0$ strongly in $Y$ and $A^*p_{\alpha_n,0}\to A^*p_0$ strongly in $X$. For every $\alpha>0$ and $w\in Y$,

$$\|p_{\alpha,w}-p_{\alpha,0}\|_Y\le\frac{\|w\|_Y}{\alpha},\qquad \|A^*p_{\alpha,w}-A^*p_{\alpha,0}\|_X\le\frac{\|A^*\|\,\|w\|_Y}{\alpha}.$$

Moreover, for any $R_0>R(u^\dagger)$ the certificate yields a variational source condition on $\{u:R(u)\le R_0\}$ with exponent $2$, coefficient $\beta=0$, and index function $\psi(s)=(1+\|p^\dagger\|_Y)\sqrt{s}$. Consequently, if $\delta_n\downarrow0$, $\|w_n\|_Y\le\delta_n$, $\alpha_n\asymp\delta_n$, and exact global minimizers $u_n$ are supplied, then the variational-source rate theorem gives

$$D_R^{A^*p^\dagger}(u_n,u^\dagger)=O(\delta_n),\qquad \|Au_n-(f+w_n)\|_Y=O(\delta_n).$$
lem-ip-tv-l2-coarea-formula:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)<\infty$. For $t>0$ set $E_t^+=\{x:u(x)>t\}$, and for $t<0$ set $E_t^-=\{x:u(x)<t\}$. Each set has finite area, almost every applicable level set has finite perimeter, and
$$TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)=\int_0^\infty P(E_t^+;\mathbb R^2)\,dt+\int_{-\infty}^0P(E_t^-;\mathbb R^2)\,dt.$$
lem-ip-tv-l2-sobolev-inequality:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Every $u\in L^2(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb R)$ with $TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2)<\infty$ satisfies
$$\|u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}\le TV_2(u;\mathbb R^2).$$
lem-ip-neumann-bv-sobolev-poincare:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For every nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, there is a finite constant $C_\Omega>0$ such that every $u\in BV(\Omega)$ satisfies
$$\|u-u_\Omega\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega),\qquad u_\Omega:=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega u\,dx.$$
lem-ip-tv-vanishing-noise-primal-compact:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $Y=L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be real Hilbert spaces. Let $A:X\to Y$ be bounded and real-linear, let $f=Au^\dagger$, and assume $u^\dagger$ is an exact solution minimizing a proper, convex, lower semicontinuous, positively one-homogeneous TV functional $R:X\to[0,+\infty]$ with a source certificate $p^\dagger\in Y$, so $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Use full-space $R=TV_2(\cdot;\mathbb R^2)$ if $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$; for a bounded connected Lipschitz $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, use either Neumann $R(u)=TV(u;\Omega)$ or Dirichlet $R(u)=TV(\widetilde u;\mathbb R^2)$ for the zero extension $\widetilde u$, assigning $+\infty$ outside the respective finite-variation domain. A bounded connected Lipschitz domain here is a bounded open set with a finite Lipschitz graph cover of its boundary, with the domain on one side of each graph, and it has no separation into two disjoint nonempty relatively open sets.

Let $\alpha_n>0$ tend to zero, let $w_n\in Y$, and suppose $\|A^*\|\,\|w_n\|_Y/\alpha_n\le\eta$ for some finite $\eta$. For each $n$, suppose a supplied global minimizer $u_n\in X$ minimizes
$$J_n(u)=\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w_n)\|_Y^2+\alpha_nR(u).$$
In the Neumann case, if $A\mathbf1_\Omega=0$, take $u_n$ after subtracting its mean $|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega u_n$; this leaves $J_n$ unchanged. Then a subsequence converges weakly in $L^2(\Omega)$ and, in addition, strongly in $L^1(\Omega)$ when $\Omega$ is bounded or strongly in $L^1$ on every bounded ball when $\Omega=\mathbb R^2$. Its limit $u_0$ is an exact solution $Au_0=f$ minimizing $R$ among exact solutions, and $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u_0)$.
lem-ip-tv-level-set-uniform-density-and-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)\to L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be bounded and real-linear, let $f=Au^\dagger$, and suppose $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-TV exact solution with a source certificate $p^\dagger$. For $\alpha_n>0$ tending to zero and noises $w_n\in L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$, assume $\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n\le\eta$ and let $u_n$ be supplied global minimizers of $\frac12\|Au-(f+w_n)\|_2^2+\alpha_n TV(u)$. Define $p_n=(f+w_n-Au_n)/\alpha_n$ and $v_n=A^*p_n$. Use $TV_2$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for full-space TV, zero-extension Dirichlet TV on a bounded Lipschitz domain, and relative Neumann TV on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain; for bounded-domain geometry use the ambient zero-extended level sets and their topological boundaries in $\mathbb R^2$.

For full-space or Dirichlet TV, assume $\eta<2\sqrt\pi$; in the bounded Dirichlet case also assume $\Omega$ has global obstacle curvature $\kappa_\Omega\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ with $\kappa_\Omega\ge g$ almost everywhere outside $\Omega$ for some $g\in L^2(\mathbb R^2\setminus\Omega)$. For Neumann TV, let $C_\Omega$ be a constant from the BV Sobolev–Poincaré inequality $\|u-u_\Omega\|_2\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega)$ and assume $\eta<1/C_\Omega$.

For almost every nonzero $t$, the level set $E_n(t)$ has finite measure and perimeter, minimizes the branch-specific perimeter minus $\int_{E}\operatorname{sgn}(t)v_n$ under compactly supported perturbations, and satisfies $P(E_n(t))=\operatorname{sgn}(t)\int_{E_n(t)}v_n$. There are constants $c>0$ and $r_0>0$, independent of $n$ and almost every such $t$, such that for every $x\in\partial E_n(t)$ and $0<r<r_0$,
$$|B(x,r)\cap E_n(t)|\ge c|B(x,r)|,\qquad |B(x,r)\setminus E_n(t)|\ge c|B(x,r)|.$$
In the full-space branch all these level sets are contained in one common ball; in the bounded branches they lie in $\overline\Omega$. The same density and support conclusions are asserted for any selected minimum-TV exact limit that carries the inherited source certificate, using zero noise. Whenever the corresponding level sets converge in measure, their canonical boundaries converge in Hausdorff distance.
thm-ip-2d-tv-level-set-convergence:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A:L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)\to L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ be bounded and real-linear, let $f=Au^\dagger$, and suppose $u^\dagger$ is a minimum-TV exact solution with a dual source certificate $p^\dagger$, meaning $A^*p^\dagger\in\partial R(u^\dagger)$. Use $R=TV_2$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for full-space TV; for a bounded connected Lipschitz domain use either Dirichlet TV of the zero extension or Neumann TV relative to $\Omega$. Let $\alpha_n>0$ tend to zero, let $w_n\in L^2(\Sigma,\mu;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\|A^*\|\|w_n\|_2/\alpha_n\le\eta$, and suppose a global minimizer $u_n$ is supplied for each functional
$$u\longmapsto\tfrac12\|Au-(f+w_n)\|_2^2+\alpha_nR(u).$$
For full-space or Dirichlet TV, assume $\eta<2\sqrt\pi$; for bounded Dirichlet TV also assume $\Omega$ has global obstacle curvature $\kappa_\Omega\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ with $\kappa_\Omega\ge g$ almost everywhere outside $\Omega$ for some $g\in L^2(\mathbb R^2\setminus\Omega)$. For Neumann TV, let $C_\Omega$ be a constant satisfying $\|u-u_\Omega\|_2\le C_\Omega TV(u;\Omega)$ on $BV(\Omega)$ and assume $\eta<1/C_\Omega$. In the Neumann case with $A\mathbf1_\Omega=0$, choose the minimizers after subtracting their means.

There is a subsequence $(u_{n_k})$ and a selected minimum-TV exact solution $u_0$ such that $Au_0=f$ and, for almost every nonzero $t$, the canonical level sets of $u_{n_k}$ converge in measure to the canonical level set of $u_0$, while their canonical ambient boundaries converge in Hausdorff distance. The limit $u_0$ need not equal the initially named truth $u^\dagger$ unless the minimum-TV exact solution is unique.
